ai.description: This snake reaches 20–30 cm. It is dark brown or purplish with a yellow lateral stripe and a blunt, shield-like tail ending in a small, bicarinate terminal scale. The head is pointed and small.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis beddomii* is best distinguished by its distinctively small, pointed head and a sharply truncated tail ending in a large, bicarinate (two-ridged) terminal shield.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis beddomii* inhabits the moist evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Beddome's earth snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through loose soil to forage for earthworms and soft-bodied invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis beddomii* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis beddomii* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at mid-to-high elevations.
